walkthroughs.body_html:
Decision Making to Improve Financial Performance — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Decision Making to Improve Financial Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Decision Making to Improve Financial Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A profitable business can still fail if it:
options: Runs out of cash to pay bills when they are due
Has too many customers
Holds a bank account
Pays its suppliers on time
The amount by which current output exceeds break-even output
The profit made on each unit
The cash held in the safe
The gap between gross and net profit

mcqs.q: Are profit and cash the same thing?
options: No - profit is revenue earned minus costs incurred, while cash is money actually flowing in and out; credit sales create profit on paper before any cash arrives.
Yes - if a business is profitable it must have plenty of cash.
Yes - profit is just the accountant's word for the bank balance.
Yes - fixed costs disappear if the factory pauses for a week.

mcqs.q: Does raising the selling price always increase total revenue?
options: Yes - customers ignore prices when buying.
Yes - a higher price per unit guarantees more revenue overall.
Yes - fixed costs disappear if the factory pauses for a week.
No - a higher price usually reduces the quantity demanded; whether revenue rises depends on price elasticity of demand.

mcqs.q: Do fixed costs fall when a business produces less?
options: Yes - all costs shrink proportionally when output drops.
Yes - fixed costs disappear if the factory pauses for a week.
No - fixed costs such as rent and salaries stay the same in the short run regardless of output; it is variable costs that change with production.
Yes - profit is just the accountant's word for the bank balance.
